Colophon how this site is made

The small print: what it’s made of, where it lives, and how to follow it.

How it’s made

The site is built with Astro into plain, static HTML. A few small parts that need to respond to you (the counting figures, the homelab readings, the triage agent, the book filter, and the timeline extras) are React components that load on their own. Everything else is just HTML and CSS.

The type is EB Garamond, a revival of Claude Garamont’s sixteenth-century types, served from this site rather than a font CDN. The navigation is set in your system’s own sans-serif. Styles are written with Tailwind CSS.

The look borrows openly from fromjason.xyz, which reads like a person rather than a portfolio.

Where it lives

It’s self-hosted on a bare-metal Linux box at home in Pune, behind Cloudflare. There is no database and no server-side code. You can see the box’s readings, and the path a request takes to reach it, on the builds page.

The site itself sets no cookies and runs no analytics. If you switch to dark mode, that choice is kept in your browser’s local storage and goes nowhere else.

Feeds & machine-readable files

  • RSS — every note, in full, for your feed reader.
  • llms.txt — a short guide to the site for language models.
  • llms-full.txt — the whole site in one Markdown file: work, case studies, books, and every note.
  • Sitemap — every public page, for search engines.
  • robots.txt — search engines and AI crawlers are welcome.
  • Raw Markdown — add .md to any note’s address for its source , like /notes/notes-from-a-pune-homelab.md .
